clinicalPearls: A chronic seronegative arthropathy that is frequently the earliest manifestation of Whipple disease, often preceding gastrointestinal symptoms by years
Typically a migratory or intermittent, non-destructive, seronegative oligo- or polyarthritis of large and medium joints
Later systemic features include weight loss, chronic diarrhoea, malabsorption, abdominal pain, lymphadenopathy and low-grade fever
Neurological and ophthalmological involvement and culture-negative endocarditis are important extra-articular manifestations
Should be suspected in a middle-aged man with unexplained seronegative arthritis who paradoxically worsens or develops systemic illness on immunosuppression
Diagnosis rests on identifying Tropheryma whipplei, classically PAS-positive macrophages on small-bowel biopsy and confirmatory PCR
Requires prolonged antibiotic therapy, often with an initial course able to penetrate the central nervous system followed by extended oral treatment
reference.pathophysiology: Whipple disease is a chronic systemic infection caused by the actinomycete Tropheryma whipplei, and the joints are among the earliest and most frequently affected sites. Although driven by an organism, the articular manifestation behaves as a seronegative inflammatory arthropathy: infiltration of tissues by bacteria-laden macrophages provokes chronic inflammation with a characteristically non-erosive, migratory joint disease. A subtle underlying defect in host macrophage handling of the organism is thought to permit persistent infection. The arthritis often long predates the classic intestinal malabsorptive phase, and immunosuppressive treatment given for a presumed primary inflammatory arthritis can accelerate the systemic disease.
additionalDifferentials: Adult-onset Still disease or other systemic inflammatory disease
additionalInvestigations: Upper gastrointestinal endoscopy with small-bowel biopsy showing PAS-positive macrophages
PCR for Tropheryma whipplei on biopsy, synovial fluid, blood or cerebrospinal fluid
Inflammatory markers (ESR, CRP) and screening for anaemia and malabsorption
Cerebrospinal fluid analysis and echocardiography to assess neurological and cardiac involvement
Rheumatoid factor and anti-CCP antibodies, characteristically negative
redFlags: Weight loss, chronic diarrhoea and malabsorption accompanying a seronegative arthritis
Neurological features (cognitive change, ophthalmoplegia, myorhythmia) suggesting CNS involvement
Paradoxical clinical deterioration after starting corticosteroids or immunosuppression
Culture-negative endocarditis in a patient with unexplained arthropathy
reference.prognosis: Untreated Whipple disease is progressive and can be fatal, but the arthropathy and systemic disease usually respond well to prolonged appropriate antibiotic therapy; central nervous system involvement carries a poorer prognosis and relapse can occur, warranting long-term follow-up.
pitfalls: Treating the arthritis as primary inflammatory disease with immunosuppression and worsening the underlying infection
Failing to consider Whipple disease in seronegative arthritis with systemic or gastrointestinal features
Relying on histology alone without confirmatory PCR
Under-treating by not addressing potential central nervous system involvement
references: Mandell, Douglas, and Bennett's Principles and Practice of Infectious Diseases
management: Treat the underlying infection with prolonged antibiotics, typically parenteral induction using ceftriaxone or penicillin followed by long-term oral co-trimoxazole
Avoid immunosuppression and biologics such as anti-TNF agents, which can accelerate or unmask systemic Whipple disease when the arthritis is misdiagnosed as a primary inflammatory arthropathy
Secure the diagnosis before treatment by demonstrating Tropheryma whipplei on small-bowel biopsy with PAS staining and confirmatory PCR
Assess for central nervous system involvement with cerebrospinal fluid PCR, as neurological disease carries a poorer prognosis and influences antibiotic choice
Provide nutritional support and correct deficiencies arising from malabsorption
Monitor the clinical and microbiological response and maintain long-term follow-up given the risk of relapse
Coordinate care across infectious diseases, rheumatology and gastroenterology
